faqs.question: Does this calendar apply to every Highlands County program?
faqs.answer: This page follows the district’s regular student calendar. Confirm separate virtual, college-course and other program requirements directly. The bell-time row covers Lake Placid High School only; other campuses may have different hours.

hero.heading: Highlands County School Calendar 2026-2027
hero.mobileDescription: First day: August 11, 2026. Last day: May 27, 2027. Winter break: December 23–January 6; January 7–8 may be make-up days.
hero.desktopDescription: Thanksgiving break is November 21–29, and spring break is March 13–21. There are six two-hour early-release dates. Students are due back January 11 after winter break unless January 7–8 are used for hurricane make-up.

editorialSummary.heading: School breaks, early releases and hurricane make-up days
paragraphs: The regular Highlands County school year began Tuesday, August 11, 2026, for students across Sebring, Avon Park and Lake Placid. The last student day is Thursday, May 27, 2027, with a two-hour early release. Thanksgiving break runs November 21–29, and spring break is March 13–21. March 26 is a separate school holiday, with regular classes scheduled March 22–25.

Winter break runs from December 23, 2026, through January 6, 2027. Students have a two-hour early release on December 22. January 7 and 8 are separate student holidays, but the district may use them as hurricane make-up days. If neither is activated, classes resume Monday, January 11. Check district notices before making plans that depend on those two dates.

The district scheduled six two-hour early releases: August 26, September 23, October 15 and December 22, 2026, plus February 11 and May 27, 2027. Under the original hurricane make-up plan, August 26, September 23, October 15 and February 11 were designated for possible conversion to full school days. The first three dates have passed; February 11 remains upcoming as of October 23, 2026. December 22 and May 27 are excluded from the conversion rule. Dismissal times vary by school.

October 16 was included in the original make-up plan, but the district announced it as a student holiday. April 23 and January 7–8 remain possible make-up days under the printed plan. The district also lists report-card distribution windows rather than a single release date for every school.
highlights: First student day: August 11, 2026; last student day: May 27, 2027.
Thanksgiving break: November 21–29; spring break: March 13–21.
Winter break: December 23–January 6, with conditional student holidays on January 7–8.
Six two-hour early releases are listed; four were originally designated for possible full-day conversion under the hurricane plan.

highlights.label: Scheduled student days
highlights.note: Published baseline: 208 weekdays minus 25 fixed closures and four scheduled student-free make-up candidates. No annual student total is printed; full-day conversions add time, while activated contact dates add attendance days.

highlights.label: Planned winter return
highlights.note: Applies if January 7-8 remain student-free. These dates may be activated under the hurricane plan.

highlights.label: Scheduled early releases
highlights.note: The hurricane plan can convert four to full days; December 22 and May 27 are exempt.

statistics.label: Student attendance days
statistics.explanation: Calculated from 208 weekdays between the first and last student days, adjusting for 25 confirmed no-school weekdays, 4 conditional make-up weekdays currently listed without regular classes. The scheduled attendance dates may change if the district activates a make-up day.

statistics.label: Confirmed non-conditional no-school weekdays
statistics.explanation: Counts 25 fixed no-class weekdays between August 11 and May 27. Excludes the four scheduled student-free make-up candidates: October 16, January 7-8 and April 23. The full published baseline has 29 no-class weekdays. Weekends and all six early-release attendance dates are excluded.

statistics.label: Listed early-release dates
statistics.explanation: Counts the six originally scheduled two-hour early-release dates: August 26, September 23, October 15 and December 22, 2026; February 11 and May 27, 2027. The original hurricane plan designated August 26, September 23, October 15 and February 11 for possible full-day conversion. As of October 23, 2026, only February 11 remains upcoming among those four. December 22 and May 27 are exempt. All six count as attendance dates in the original calendar; converting an early release adds instructional time, not another attendance date.

statistics.label: Longest listed break
statistics.explanation: Dec 23, 2026–Jan 6, 2027, including weekends. The stretch contains 11 confirmed no-school weekdays.

statistics.label: Long weekends from fixed holidays
statistics.explanation: Counts four long weekends formed by unconditional weekday closures in the original board-approved calendar: September 5–7, January 16–18, February 12–14 and March 26–28. October 16 was separately announced as a student holiday but is excluded from this fixed-calendar count because it was originally a hurricane make-up candidate. April 23 remains conditional.

statistics.label: Full-week breaks
statistics.explanation: Counts continuous no-school stretches containing at least five confirmed weekdays without regular classes. Adjacent holidays and weekends remain part of the same break.

comparativeInsights: The 15-day break statistic counts fixed time off from December 23 through January 6. The planned 19-day winter stretch also depends on January 7-8 remaining student-free.

schoolHours.scope: Lake Placid High School - 2026-2027 A/B days and C days
schoolHours.note: A/B days begin with study hall. Study hall exemption rules apply; confirm your student’s required arrival time with the school. These hours do not establish another campus’s schedule or a universal shortened-day clock.

events.name: First Day of School for Students
Two-Hour Early Release
events.note: Two-hour early release was scheduled for this attendance day. The district's August reminder also announced earlier bus arrivals. This date was eligible for conversion to a full day under the printed hurricane make-up plan.

events.name: Two-Hour Early Release
events.note: Two-hour early release was scheduled. Lake Placid High's September 23 notice specified no study hall, an 8:34 a.m. class start and 1:30 p.m. dismissal. Those times apply only to Lake Placid High on that date. September 23 was also eligible for full-day conversion under the printed hurricane plan.

events.name: Two-Hour Early Release
events.note: The district announced a two-hour early release. Sebring High specified 1:25 p.m. dismissal on October 15; other campuses had their own dismissal times. This date was eligible for full-day conversion under the printed hurricane plan.

events.name: Student Holiday and Teacher Workday
events.note: October 16 was a scheduled student holiday and teacher workday, confirmed by the district's October reminder. The original calendar also listed it as a possible hurricane make-up day. That designation is historical, not a pending schedule change.

events.name: Report Card Distribution Window
events.note: The calendar gives a distribution window; confirm your school’s release day or online availability.

events.name: Thanksgiving Break
events.note: The district marks November 21–29 as a holiday, including both weekends. Students have no regular classes November 23–27, with school scheduled to resume November 30.

events.name: Two-Hour Early Release and End of First Semester
events.officialLabel: Early Release (TWD) / End of nine weeks (semester)
events.note: Students attend school with dismissal two hours early. This date ends the second nine weeks and the first semester. December 22 is expressly exempt from full-day conversion under the hurricane make-up plan.

events.name: Student Holiday and Teacher Workday
events.note: Scheduled student holiday and teacher workday. January 7–8 may be used as hurricane make-up school days. The district's printed plan does not specify an order between the two dates.

events.name: Student Holiday / Staff Professional Development
events.note: Scheduled student holiday and staff professional development day. January 7–8 may be used as hurricane make-up school days. The printed plan gives no separate priority between these dates.

events.name: Report Card Distribution Window
events.note: This is a reporting window, not daily report-card delivery or a change to attendance. It spans a weekend and the January 18 holiday; check your school’s release date or online availability.

events.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Day (No School)
Two-Hour Early Release and Progress Reports
events.officialLabel: Early Release (PD) / Progress Reports go home
events.note: Two-hour early release and progress-report distribution share this date. Students attend school, but the hurricane make-up plan allows the early release to be converted to a full day.

events.name: Report Card Distribution Window
events.note: The district lists March 29–31 and April 1–2 as adjacent report-card dates. They are combined here into one distribution window, not five separate report-card releases. This window does not mean classes are canceled.

events.name: Holiday (Possible Hurricane Make-Up Day)
events.note: April 23 is a holiday with no regular student classes on the published calendar, but it may be activated as a hurricane make-up day. The printed plan places it after October 16 and before January 7–8, regardless of chronological order. Confirm district notices before relying on the day off.

events.name: Last Day of School — Two-Hour Early Release
events.officialLabel: Students Last day / Early Release / End of Nine Weeks
events.note: The final regular student day also ends the fourth nine weeks. Schools dismiss two hours early. May 27 is expressly exempt from full-day conversion under the hurricane make-up plan.

breaks.name: October long weekend (student holiday announced)
breaks.note: The district's October reminder announced October 16 as a student holiday, followed by the October 17–18 weekend. October 15 had scheduled early-release attendance. The original calendar also listed October 16 as a hurricane make-up candidate; that contingency is retained as historical context, not a pending activation. This records the announced schedule rather than independently verified actual attendance.

breaks.name: Thanksgiving holiday
breaks.schoolWeekdaysOffNote: The official holiday already includes both weekends. It contains five no-class weekdays, November 23-27; no extra Thanksgiving make-up designation is printed.

breaks.name: Winter break and January student holidays (make-up days possible)
breaks.note: The named Winter Break is December 23-January 6. January 7-8 are separate student holidays that may become make-up attendance days. If they stay student-free, the next scheduled class day is January 11, and the full stretch is 19 calendar days including the January 9-10 weekend. There are 11 fixed Winter Break weekdays and two conditional weekdays; confirm any hurricane instructions.

breaks.name: February long weekend
breaks.schoolWeekdaysOffNote: February 12 is a student holiday and teacher workday. The following weekend makes three days without regular classes. February 15 is a scheduled school day.

breaks.name: Spring break
breaks.schoolWeekdaysOffNote: The official Spring Break already includes both weekends. It contains five no-class weekdays, March 15-19. March 22-25 are scheduled classes before the separate March 26 holiday.

breaks.name: April long weekend (make-up day possible)
breaks.note: The published holiday and weekend give a planned three-day stretch. April 23 may become a student contact day under the hurricane plan; confirm district instructions.

A complete district calendar image published with Sebring High’s May 18 announcement was also reviewed and agrees with its dates, legend, approval and make-up rules. Direct Google downloads timed out, so remote PDF byte identity has not been established. Current available official News and Live Feed content provides school-specific schedule context.
about.processing: Read extracted text and the full rendered page. Red underlined dates mean two-hour early release; vertical stripes mean nine-week endings, yellow means holiday and diagonal strokes mean no school for students with teacher work/development. August 26, September 23, October 15, December 22, February 11 and May 27 are the six early releases. The first four dates named in the hurricane conversion rule exclude December 22 and May 27, leaving August 26/September 23/October 15/February 11 eligible for full-day conversion. They remain attendance dates, with the rule recorded in notes rather than in conditional no-school IDs. October 16, April 23 and January 7-8 are the four additional possible contact dates and retain explicit published-no-class conditional fields. Preserve the printed make-up priority: eligible early releases, October 16, April 23, then January 7-8; do not replace it with chronological order or invent an order within the January pair. February 12 is a fixed student holiday, not a listed hurricane reserve; February 15 is white/scheduled attendance. Thanksgiving November 21-29 and Spring Break March 13-21 already include weekends. Winter has separate official December 23-31 and January 1-6 captions; retain both. Its planned continuous span includes conditional January 7-8 and the following weekend, so the weekday-off count is withheld and January 11 return is explicitly conditional/derived. December 21-22 are attendance. Do not bridge March 22-25 to the March 26 holiday. Report cards are three distribution windows, not daily issue events or closures. Keep January 11-22 intact as the printed reporting window with an explicit January 18 holiday caveat. Merge only the truly adjacent March 29-31 and April 1-2 captions into a derived five-weekday reporting range. February 11 early release and progress reports share one canonical event. December 22 also ends the second nine weeks and explicitly the semester; May 27 combines last day, early release and fourth-nine-week end without inventing a separately labeled semester end. Derived baseline attendance is 208 weekdays minus 25 fixed closures and four scheduled student-free reserves, or 179; no annual total is printed. Pre-year staff dates, May 28 workday and post-year May 31 holiday are excluded. October 7, 2025 printed Board approval is used; April 2026 PDF metadata is not an announced revision. The 2026-2027 Lake Placid High bell graphic and full April 27 notice establish school-scoped regular hours, including study hall exemptions; no generic district clock or inferred exemption arrival time is published. Date-specific September 23 Lake Placid 1:30 and October 15 Sebring 1:25 releases stay in their event notes, not as a current districtwide clock. The August 26 bus/afterschool-care notice is date-scoped; later childcare availability is not assumed.

faqs.question: When does school start in Highlands County for 2026-2027?
faqs.answer: The first day of school for students is Tuesday, August 11, 2026. This date comes from the School Board of Highlands County's regular student calendar. Individual schools provide their own arrival, orientation and bus information.

faqs.question: When is the last day of school in Highlands County in 2027?
faqs.answer: Thursday, May 27, 2027, is the last student day. Schools have a two-hour early release that day, which also marks the end of the fourth nine-week grading period. May 28 is a teacher workday, not another student attendance day.

faqs.question: When is Thanksgiving break for Highlands County schools in 2026?
faqs.answer: Thanksgiving break runs November 21–29, 2026, including both weekends. Students have no classes Monday, November 23, through Friday, November 27. Classes are scheduled to resume Monday, November 30.

faqs.question: When is winter break for Highlands County schools in 2026-2027?
faqs.answer: The district's official winter break is December 23, 2026, through January 6, 2027. December 22 is still a school day, with dismissal two hours early. January 7–8 are separate student holidays, not part of the dates officially labeled Winter Break.

faqs.question: When do Highlands County students return after winter break in January 2027?
faqs.answer: Monday, January 11, 2027, is the planned return date if January 7 and 8 remain student holidays. Both dates are listed as possible hurricane make-up days, so students could be required to return earlier if the district activates them. Check district announcements before relying on January 11.

faqs.question: Is there school on December 21 and December 22, 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both Monday, December 21, and Tuesday, December 22, are scheduled school days. December 22 has a two-hour early release and marks the end of the first semester. Winter break begins December 23.

faqs.question: Does Highlands County have a fall break in October 2026?
faqs.answer: The district did not schedule a week-long fall break. Students had a planned two-hour early release on October 15, followed by a student holiday on October 16. The district also issued a no-school reminder for October 16. Although that date appeared in the original hurricane make-up plan, it is now a historical contingency, not a pending schedule change.

faqs.question: Are Highlands County schools closed on Labor Day 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes. Monday, September 7, 2026, was marked as a no-school holiday on the district calendar.

faqs.question: Is there school on Veterans Day in Highlands County in 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes. Wednesday, November 11, 2026, is a regular school day on the published district calendar. It is not listed as a student holiday or early-release date.

faqs.question: Do Highlands County students have Martin Luther King Jr. Day off in 2027?
faqs.answer: Yes. Monday, January 18, 2027, is a school holiday, with no regular classes.

faqs.question: Is there school on Friday, February 12, 2027?
faqs.answer: No. February 12 is a student holiday for a teacher workday. Students have a two-hour early release on Thursday, February 11, followed by a three-day weekend from February 12 through February 14.

faqs.question: Are Highlands County schools open on Presidents Day, February 15, 2027?
faqs.answer: Yes. Monday, February 15, 2027, is a scheduled school day. Although it is the federal Presidents Day holiday, the district's published student calendar does not mark February 15 as a day off.

faqs.question: When is spring break for Highlands County schools in 2027?
faqs.answer: Spring break runs March 13–21, 2027, including both weekends. Students have no classes March 15–19 and are scheduled to return Monday, March 22.

faqs.question: Are Highlands County schools closed on Good Friday, March 26, 2027?
faqs.answer: Yes. Friday, March 26, 2027, falls on Good Friday, and the district calendar marks that date as a school holiday. The calendar labels it simply "Holiday" rather than "Good Friday." It is separate from spring break, which ends March 21. Classes are scheduled March 22–25 and resume Monday, March 29.

faqs.question: Is there school on Friday, April 23, 2027?
faqs.answer: April 23 is a scheduled school holiday, but the district may use it as a hurricane make-up day. The published calendar does not make that change automatic. Check district announcements before treating the date as a guaranteed day off.

faqs.question: What are the two-hour early-release dates for Highlands County schools in 2026-2027?
faqs.answer: The six dates are August 26, September 23, October 15 and December 22, 2026, followed by February 11 and May 27, 2027. The original hurricane plan identified August 26, September 23, October 15 and February 11 as possible full-day conversion dates. December 22 and May 27 are exempt. Of the eligible dates, only February 11 remains upcoming as of October 23, 2026.

faqs.question: What time do Highlands County schools dismiss on early-release days?
faqs.answer: Dismissal times depend on the school; the district specifies a two-hour reduction rather than one universal dismissal time. For example, Sebring High announced 1:25 p.m. dismissal for October 15, 2026, while Lake Placid High announced 1:30 p.m. for September 23. Those times apply only to the named schools and dates. Check your school's announcement for each early release.

faqs.question: Do buses and after-school care change on early-release days?
faqs.answer: Families should plan for earlier pickup and bus arrivals. For the August 26, 2026, early release, the district announced that buses would arrive home two hours earlier than usual and that elementary after-school care was available for pre-registered students. That notice does not guarantee the same childcare arrangements on every date. Confirm transportation and care with your school.

faqs.question: How does Highlands County make up school days missed because of hurricanes?
faqs.answer: The district's printed plan first allows eligible two-hour early releases to become full school days, excluding December 22 and May 27. It then lists October 16, April 23 and finally January 7–8 as possible additional attendance days. October 16 has already passed and was announced as a student holiday. As of October 23, 2026, February 11, January 7–8 and April 23 remain future dates that could be affected by district make-up decisions. These changes are not automatic.

faqs.question: When do Highlands County students receive progress reports in 2026-2027?
faqs.answer: Progress reports are scheduled to go home September 11 and November 13, 2026, and February 11 and April 22, 2027. February 11 is also a two-hour early-release day.

faqs.question: When are Highlands County report cards sent home in 2026-2027?
faqs.answer: The district lists report-card distribution windows of October 19–23, 2026; January 11–22, 2027; and March 29–April 2, 2027. These are reporting windows, not daily report-card releases. The January window includes the January 18 school holiday. Check your school for its actual release date or online availability. The annual calendar does not list a separate final fourth-quarter report-card date.

faqs.question: When do the nine-week grading periods and first semester end?
faqs.answer: The four nine-week grading periods end October 9 and December 22, 2026, and March 12 and May 27, 2027. December 22 is explicitly marked as the end of the first semester. Both December 22 and May 27 have two-hour early release, but October 9 and March 12 are not listed as early-release dates.

faqs.question: How many student attendance days are scheduled in Highlands County for 2026-2027?
faqs.answer: The published calendar works out to 179 student attendance dates under the original schedule, although the district does not print an official annual total. There are 208 weekdays from August 11 through May 27, with 29 originally scheduled as days without regular classes. Four of those 29 were designated as possible hurricane make-up dates. Turning an early-release day into a full day adds instructional time, not another attendance date.

faqs.question: Do all Highlands County schools have the same start and dismissal times?
faqs.answer: No. Schools have their own bell schedules. Lake Placid High School's posted 2026-2027 A/B-day and C-day schedules run from 8:34 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., with study hall exemptions affecting some students. Those hours should not be used for other campuses. Check your child's school for its actual arrival and dismissal times.

faqs.question: Does the Highlands County school calendar apply to every school and program?
faqs.answer: This page follows the School Board of Highlands County's regular student calendar. Individual schools may have different bell times, activities and senior schedules. Families using Highlands Virtual, dual-enrollment courses or other specialized programs should confirm any separate attendance and course requirements with their school or program.

faqs.question: Where can I find Highlands County high school graduation dates for 2027?
faqs.answer: The district's regular 2026-2027 calendar does not list graduation ceremony dates or separate senior attendance deadlines. Check announcements from Avon Park High School, Lake Placid High School, Sebring High School or the relevant virtual program for confirmed ceremony dates and senior instructions.

faqs.question: Where can I find the official Highlands County school calendar and schedule updates?
faqs.answer: Visit the School Board of Highlands County's official Calendar page or use the district calendar PDF linked on this page. For changes to hurricane make-up days, early dismissal, transportation or school-specific events, also check district News, Live Feed and announcements from your child's school.
